Université Grenoble Alpes (#387 (QS 2027)) does engineering, physics, computer science and environmental science in the cheapest student city here. The University of Strasbourg (#456 (QS 2027)) lists 98 English-taught master’s, more than any other university on this page.

The University of Bordeaux (#485 (QS 2027)) covers medicine, law, engineering and viticulture. Aix-Marseille Université (#443 (QS 2027)) is the largest here at 80,000 students, in a city costing €850–1,300 per month. Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1 (#613 (QS 2027)) is medicine, pharmacy and life sciences. The University of Lille (#686 (QS 2027)) gives first-time non-EU master’s entrants an automatic waiver, so they pay €254 per year — the cheapest master’s route on this list.

## English-taught programmes [...] Université Paris Cité (#300 (QS 2026)) exonerates every non-EU entrant to €178 per year, and is the main Paris address for medicine, pharmacy, public health and psychology.

Sciences Po (#354 (QS 2027)) is public but prices independently: €14,900 per year flat for non-EEA students, for political science, international relations, public affairs, law and journalism. It lists 3 English-taught bachelor’s, one of the few places in France that does.

HEC Paris teaches its master’s entirely in English at €29,450 per year, in Jouy-en-Josas outside Paris, where campus rooms cost €560–780 per month. ESSEC Business School in Cergy charges €15,900 per year for its Global BBA and also admits through its Rabat campus. [...] ## Tuition and scholarships

At a public university the published non-EU rate is €178–2,902 per year for a Licence and €255–3,950 per year for a master’s, plus the compulsory CVEC contribution of €105 per year, paid once at enrolment. Where you land inside those bands is decided by the university, not by you: Paris Cité and Paris-Saclay exonerate all non-EU entrants to the bottom, Lille does it automatically for first-time master’s entrants, Bordeaux and Strasbourg do it case by case on merit or need, and Aix-Marseille, Lyon 1 and Grenoble Alpes charge the top.

A May 2026 decree changed the arithmetic: the exemption quotas were widened, but eligibility was cut back to individual financial-hardship cases, ending blanket institutional exemptions. Expect the picture to tighten for 2027/28.

### Typical duration

Masters in France mostly take between 1 year and 2 years to complete.

### Typical tuition fees

At public universities, students from the EU/EEA pay either €243 or €601 per year, and other international students pay €3,770. At private universities and business schools, fees are higher, up to around €25,000 per year.

   The application process for Master’s degrees in France depends on a few main factors: your nationality, your current country of residence, and which type of institution(s) you want to apply to.

   For public universities, it works like this: [...] To apply for a Master’s degree in France, you typically need to prepare the following documents:

    Undergraduate degree certificate (for degrees obtained outside France, a translation into French might be required)
    Proof of English skills (such as IELTS or TOEFL score certificates)
    A detailed curriculum vitae / résumé
    A personal statement describing your personal and career goals
    References or letters of recommendation
    For non-EU students: a copy of their photo ID/passport, or a copy of the residency permit (carte de séjour), or a confirmation of receipt of the residency permit application for the current year
    Overview of personal work (portfolio, bibliography, thesis, research project, etc.)
    Questionnaire by the university
